conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Fourier Epicycles
style.description: A chain of spinning brass arms on a drafting table: each arm turns at a whole-number speed on the end of the last, each with its circle drawn as a thin brass ring, and a coral-tipped pen at the end of the chain leaves a blue-black ink line on cream paper. The arms are the terms of a discrete Fourier transform of a closed outline (epicycles.js: arc-length resampling, DFT in plain JS, terms sorted by size), so one arm draws a circle, a few draw a lumpy loop and sixty draw the picture. The ink line is the same finite sum evaluated up to the current phase; earlier, coarser outlines stay on the paper in faint grey. Bright warm daylight, brass, ink blue-black and one coral accent.
motion: Every arm turns at a whole-number speed k (once per cycle for k = 1, twice for k = 2, backwards for negative k) on the end of the arm before it; the pen is the sum of all arms.
The ink line is the same finite Fourier sum evaluated from phase 0 up to the current phase — never accumulated; each drawing is exactly one full turn.
New arms unfurl largest first (length 0 -> r with a small overshoot) while the pen is lifted; the previous outline fades to faint grey.
Arms are stacked one on the end of the last; tiny outer arms keep a minimum on-screen width, rings a minimum line width.

notes.mechanism: epicycles.js: an original songbird outline (33 control points, closed Hermite spline) resampled to 256 points by arc length; DFT in plain JS with a sqrt-only twiddle table (bit-identical in Node and Chrome); c_0 is the pivot, the other 255 terms sorted by amplitude. Beat k shows the first K terms; the pen is their sum at the beat's phase, the ink is that sum sampled over one turn and drawn up to the current phase.
